{
  "title": "Layout-Structured Multi-Hop Evidence Chains for Complex Document Reasoning",
  "project_name": "layout_hop_evidence_chain",
  "source": "web_research",
  "core_problem": "Complex document questions require synthesizing evidence from multiple layout regions within a single page — reading a value from a table, referencing the adjacent caption, then cross-checking with an embedded chart — but no existing method trains a generative VLM to produce explicit multi-hop traversal traces across Table, Figure, Caption, and TextBlock nodes while preserving typed spatial relationships between semantic layout elements. Models either flatten the document into a token sequence (losing inter-region structure) or navigate page-by-page (missing within-page region-to-region links), or use implicit graph propagation with no supervisable chain-of-thought.

The empirical gap is well-established for WITHIN-PAGE multi-hop layout reasoning: WikiMixQA (arXiv:2506.15594, ACL 2025 Findings) demonstrates that within-page multi-hop table-and-chart reasoning is severely challenging for current models — GPT-4o is the only model exceeding 50% accuracy even in the direct-context setting, while open-source models max at 27% in retrieval settings. InfographicVQA's hard multi-hop layout questions (requiring ≥2 layout-region hops across charts, tables, captions, and text blocks in a single infographic) represent a second per-page evaluation front where base VLMs that treat pages as flat images fail to exploit spatial relationships.

Two prior works come closest. PDF-VQA (arXiv:2304.06447, ECML-PKDD 2023) already builds typed Logical Relation graphs (parent-child hierarchical) and Spatial Relation graphs (8-directional: top/bottom/left/right and four diagonals) over document nodes including title, text, list, figure, table, table caption, and figure caption — graph construction over these node types is therefore not novel. But PDF-VQA's LoSpa model is fully extractive (predicts an element index via GCN, then retrieves OCR text from that region), produces no verbalized traversal chain-of-thought, and is evaluated only on the proprietary PDF-VQA PubMed dataset. MGA-VQA (arXiv:2511.17881, NeurIPS 2025) builds a spatial graph from OCR-detected text bounding boxes with untyped proximity/similarity edges and propagates through a 3-layer implicit GCN; its text-box nodes miss figure and chart regions entirely, its edges carry no semantic type labels, and all outputs are extractive spans with no traversal chain-of-thought.

The structured gap is: no method trains a generative VLM to verbalize step-by-step multi-hop traversal across typed layout-region nodes within a page — the exact capability required to answer questions that chain a table value through an Adjacent edge to its Caption and then through a Caption-of edge into a referenced Figure.",
  "opportunity": "InfographicVQA (WACV 2022, leaderboard active) is the primary required evaluation target: it is genuinely per-page and layout-intensive, requiring joint reasoning over charts, tables, maps, and text blocks within single infographic images. Qwen2.5-VL-7B self-reports 82.6% ANLS on the InfoVQA test set, but the actual fine-tuning backbone is Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, whose InfoVQA baseline must be established via zero-shot evaluation on Day 1 of the project (the Thinking variant reports 86.0% InfoVQA test, so the Instruct baseline is likely in the 84–87% range). Regardless of the overall ANLS level, hard multi-hop layout questions — those requiring the model to traverse ≥2 typed layout regions to compose the answer — remain a defensible hard subset where LHEC's explicit traversal training targets a meaningful gap over the base model.

WikiMixQA (arXiv:2506.15594, ACL 2025 Findings) is the primary required secondary evaluation target: it benchmarks within-page multi-hop reasoning over table+chart pairs from Wikipedia, finding that GPT-4o is the only model exceeding 50% accuracy even in the direct-context setting, while open-source VLMs max at 27% in retrieval settings. This directly quantifies the within-page typed-region traversal gap that LHEC targets with its Adjacent and Caption-of edges, and provides a non-ceiling evaluation target where strong gains are expected.

DocHop-QA (arXiv:2508.15851, NeurIPS 2025 track) is explicitly a cross-DOCUMENT benchmark (its own paper reports multi-document reasoning dominates overall). LHEC's per-page graphs cannot address cross-document failure modes. DocHop-QA is therefore used ONLY as a supplementary training corpus after a Day 1 audit: instances where all BBox-annotated evidence regions fall within a single page are extracted and used for within-page traversal chain synthesis; the cross-document majority of the 11,379 instances is excluded. If the within-page audit yields fewer than 500 usable instances, DocHop-QA is dropped from training entirely and the claim of using it is removed.

BRIDGE (March 2026, arXiv:2603.07931) provides grounded multi-hop evidence annotations for long scientific documents and confirms no proposed method resolves the within-page cross-region gap it diagnoses; it is a strong secondary evaluation target for the AAAI 2027 extended version. The combination of DocLayout-YOLO layout detection + rule-based typed graph + generative VLM fine-tuned on explicit verbalized traversal chains is architecturally distinct from PDF-VQA (extractive element-index model) and MGA-VQA (implicit GCN on OCR boxes), buildable entirely from open components, and executable within 15 days targeting EMNLP 2026 ARR (May 25, 2026).",
  "landscape": "Multi-page document VQA methods include GRAM (learnable document tokens), Hi-VT5 (hierarchical page summaries), Doc-V* (April 2026, arXiv:2604.13731, coarse-to-fine agentic page navigation), AVIR (Jan 2026, adaptive visual retrieval for SlideVQA). Within-page multi-hop reasoning: ARGUS (CVPR 2025) grounds single visual elements with bounding boxes in CoT chains; GCoT (March 2025) generates coordinate-grounded reasoning steps; MAGIC-VQA (ACL 2025 Findings) uses commonsense knowledge graphs for inference.

PDF-VQA (arXiv:2304.06447, ECML-PKDD 2023) is an important predecessor that must be cited and differentiated from. It builds both a typed Logical Relation graph (LR graph: binary parent-child hierarchical edges) and a typed Spatial Relation graph (SR graph: 8-directional edges — top, bottom, left, right, top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right) over document element nodes including title, text, list, figure, table, table caption, and figure caption — the same node types LHEC uses. Its LoSpa model propagates via GCN to predict the index of the document element containing the answer (fully extractive: answer is OCR text retrieved from that region). PDF-VQA is evaluated only on its own proprietary PubMed Central dataset and contains no verbalized chain-of-thought. LHEC's novel contribution relative to PDF-VQA is the training of a generative VLM to verbalize traversal traces step-by-step ('Table[3]→[Adjacent]→Caption[4]→[Caption-of]→Figure[5]') as a directly supervisable chain-of-thought.

MGA-VQA (Nov 2025, arXiv:2511.17881, NeurIPS 2025 track) is the second closest prior work and the most important direct comparison target: it uses OCR-detected text boxes as nodes (no figure/chart nodes), untyped proximity and semantic-similarity edges with scalar weights, a 3-layer GCN for implicit propagation, and extractive span outputs; it evaluates on FUNSD, CORD, SROIE, DocVQA, STE-VQA, RICO — DocVQA is included but all outputs are extractive spans from OCR boxes; no verbalized traversal chain-of-thought is produced and figure/chart regions are invisible to the model. LHEC differentiates on four axes: semantic layout region nodes, typed edges, verbalized traversal traces, and generative output. Public code at github.com/ahmad-shirazi/MGAVQA enables direct comparison.

GraphDoc (ICLR 2025) annotates spatial and logical relations (Up/Down/Left/Right, Parent/Child/Sequence) between document nodes, providing the taxonomy directly used in LHEC's rule-based edge assignment.

WikiMixQA (arXiv:2506.15594, ACL 2025 Findings) benchmarks within-page multi-hop reasoning over table+chart pairs from Wikipedia: GPT-4o is the only model >50% accuracy in direct-context settings; open-source VLMs max at 27% in retrieval settings. This benchmark directly targets the within-page typed-region traversal gap that LHEC addresses with its Adjacent and Caption-of edges.

HopChain (March 2026, arXiv:2603.17024) synthesizes multi-hop vision-language reasoning data for RLVR training via category identification, instance segmentation, multi-hop query generation, and verifiable numeric answers — it is a counting-task synthesis framework, NOT a document layout traversal chain method, and is not used in LHEC's synthesis pipeline. LHEC's traversal chain synthesis is a custom pipeline described separately.

DocHop-QA (Aug 2025, arXiv:2508.15851, NeurIPS 2025 track) is a cross-DOCUMENT benchmark where multi-document reasoning dominates; it is NOT suitable as a primary LHEC evaluation target since LHEC's per-page graphs cannot address cross-document reasoning. DocHop-QA's BBox-annotated evidence regions are useful as a supplementary within-page training source after auditing for single-page-evidence instances only.

Benchmark papers BRIDGE (March 2026) and DocHop-QA (Aug 2025) diagnose the multi-hop gap without proposing methods. InfographicVQA (WACV 2022): Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct zero-shot baseline to be established on Day 1; Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking reports 86.0% ANLS on InfoVQA test; the hard multi-hop layout question subset where ≥2 typed region hops are required remains the primary evaluation target where LHEC is expected to show improvement.",
  "approach": "We propose LHEC (Layout-Structured Hop Evidence Chains): given a document page, DocLayout-YOLO detects all layout regions (TextBlock, Table, Figure, Caption), and rule-based heuristics assign typed spatial and semantic edges to build a per-page evidence graph — no separate relation head training is required, eliminating a 2-4 day training dependency. Specifically: (1) Caption-of edge: from a Caption node to the nearest Table or Figure within 150px vertical distance; (2) Adjacent edge: between any two regions sharing a column or row boundary within 50px; (3) Up/Down/Left/Right edges: from center-point geometry following GraphDoc taxonomy (nearest neighbor in each axis direction). This rule-based assignment is deterministic, requires no annotated training data, and completes in minutes on CPU alongside DocLayout-YOLO inference. A trained relation head replacing these heuristics is a natural extension presented as future work (AAAI 2027 version).

A Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct backbone fine-tuned with QLoRA is trained to produce structured multi-hop reasoning traces that explicitly traverse this graph — citing region node IDs and edge types at each hop (e.g., 'Table[3]→[Adjacent]→Caption[4]→[Caption-of]→Figure[5]') — before producing the final answer.

Training data synthesis (custom pipeline — not HopChain, which is a numeric counting RLVR framework unrelated to document layout traversal): (1) Run DocLayout-YOLO over InfographicVQA training images and PMC-OA scientific page subset to detect Table/Figure/Caption/TextBlock regions. (2) Align ground-truth QA evidence regions to detected layout nodes via IoU overlap ≥ 0.5; when IoU < 0.5, assign the evidence span to the nearest detected region by centroid distance. (3) Build the per-page typed evidence graph with rule-based edges (Caption-of, Adjacent, Up/Down/Left/Right). (4) For each QA pair, extract the shortest path in the evidence graph traversing all aligned evidence regions — this forms the traversal template. (5) Verbalize the traversal template into a structured chain-of-thought: 'Table[3]→[Adjacent]→Caption[4]→[Caption-of]→Figure[5]' covering 2-4 hop lengths. The InfographicVQA training split (~24K QA pairs) is the primary training source — it is per-page, layout-intensive, and in-distribution with respect to the primary evaluation target. PMC-OA scientific pages supplement this corpus with figure+caption+table triplets characteristic of academic document layouts.

DocHop-QA is audited on Day 1 for within-page-amenable instances (all evidence BBox regions on a single page). If this audit yields ≥500 instances, they are included as a supplementary training source. If fewer than 500 instances qualify (expected given cross-document dominance), DocHop-QA is dropped from training and this decision is documented in the paper.

For the EMNLP 2026 submission, cross-page PageRef linking is scoped out — per-page graphs are used throughout; rule-based cross-reference linking is explicitly presented as future work for the AAAI 2027 extended version.

Evaluation plan:
(1) Day 1 prerequisite: Zero-shot Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct evaluation on InfographicVQA and WikiMixQA to establish actual baselines. This is a precondition for interpretable contribution framing — the paper cannot use the 82.6% ANLS figure from Qwen2.5-VL-7B as the baseline for a different backbone.
(2) Primary benchmark: InfographicVQA (per-page, layout-intensive, active leaderboard). Report: (a) overall ANLS, base Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct vs. LHEC-fine-tuned; (b) hard multi-hop layout subset ANLS (questions requiring ≥2 typed region hops, identified by automatic annotation over answer-source categories), where the largest gains are expected.
(3) Required secondary benchmark: WikiMixQA (within-page table+chart multi-hop, ACL 2025 Findings; direct-context setting). Strong gains expected given open-source models at ≤27–50% range — this is the non-ceiling target that most directly demonstrates LHEC's typed traversal advantage.
(4) Scope-acknowledged secondary benchmark: DocHop-QA within-page-only subset (after audit). Report LHEC vs. base model on this subset with explicit framing: 'LHEC addresses within-page layout traversal; results are reported on the ~X% of DocHop-QA instances where all evidence is contained within a single page.'
(5) Regression checks: DocVQA (~96% for base, near ceiling — regression check only), ChartQA (near ceiling — regression check only).
(6) Zero-shot general regression suite: TextVQA, GQA, POPE, MMBench, SEED-Bench, RealWorldQA — base Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct vs. fine-tuned LHEC, confirming no general regression from document-specific QLoRA fine-tuning.

Baselines: vanilla Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct (zero-shot), ARGUS (single-element grounding), PDF-VQA LoSpa (extractive element-selection, re-implemented on DocHop-QA within-page subset and InfographicVQA), MGA-VQA (direct comparison using public codebase on InfographicVQA and WikiMixQA).",

## Reviewer feedback (round 4)
Issues: ["EVALUATION SETTING AMBIGUITY — WikiMixQA: The 27% figure cited throughout is for open-source models in the RETRIEVAL setting (where models must locate the relevant page). LHEC operates in the DIRECT-CONTEXT setting (the page image is given). From the WikiMixQA paper, proprietary models achieve ~70% in direct-context, implying open-source models likely score in the 40–55% range direct-context. The generator must (a) specify that LHEC is evaluated in the direct-context setting, (b) establish the Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct zero-shot direct-context baseline on Day 1 alongside the InfoVQA baseline, and (c) restate the expected gain accordingly. Claiming gains from a 27% retrieval-setting floor when LHEC targets direct-context is misleading.", "MISSING CITATION — LayoutLLM/LayoutCoT (CVPR 2024): LayoutLLM introduces a LayoutCoT module that generates layout-aware chain-of-thought supervision for document understanding (DocVQA +1.96%, FUNSD +5.96%), and is directly related work the generator has omitted. EMNLP reviewers familiar with this line will immediately flag the gap. LHEC's differentiation is clear and compelling — LayoutCoT uses text-based layout CoT without explicit spatial graph nodes or traversal notation; LHEC uses typed layout-region graphs with node-ID traversal chains ('Table[3]→[Adjacent]→Caption[4]') — but this must be stated in the landscape section.", "UNDERDEFINED PRIMARY EVALUATION SUBSET — InfographicVQA hard multi-hop subset: The paper's contribution framing depends critically on gains within the hard multi-hop layout question subset (≥2 typed region hops), but the proposal does not specify: (a) how many InfographicVQA test questions qualify (if fewer than ~150, statistical significance claims are questionable), (b) whether this subset is defined by existing InfographicVQA answer-source category annotations or requires new annotation, and (c) what the base model's performance on this subset is prior to fine-tuning. Without a well-defined, sufficiently large subset, the claim of targeted improvement is unverifiable.", "DOCLAYOUT-YOLO DETECTION QUALITY ON INFOGRAPHICS — No concrete pre-validation plan: DocLayout-YOLO was trained primarily on academic-style documents (PubLayNet, DocLayNet). ### Overview
LayoutLLM is an LLM/MLLM based method for document understanding, with a core focus on layout instruction tuning strategy specially designed to enhance the comprehension and utilization of document layouts.

### Key Components
The proposed layout instruction tuning strategy consists of two components: Layout-aware Pre-training and Layout-aware Supervised Fine-tuning. To capture the characteristics of document layout in Layout-aware Pre-training, three groups of pre-training tasks, corresponding to document-level, region-level and segment-level information, are introduced.

### LayoutCoT Module
A novel module called layout chain-of-thought (LayoutCoT) is devised to enable LayoutLLM to focus on regions relevant to the question and generate accurate answers. Unlike existing methods that are directly supervised by the answer to the document understanding question, LayoutCoT consists of three successive steps: Question Analysis, Relevant Area Concentration, and Answer Formation.

### Performance and Benefits
LayoutCoT is effective for boosting the performance of document understanding and brings a certain degree of interpretability, which could facilitate manual inspection and correction. Experiments on standard benchmarks show that the proposed LayoutLLM significantly outperforms existing methods that adopt open-source 7B LLMs/MLLMs for document understanding.

# WikiMixQA Benchmark: Model Performance Analysis

## Accuracy Numbers

**Direct-Context Setting (Oracle):**
- GPT-4o: 71.42%

- GPT-4o: 55.24%
- Gemini-2.0-Pro: 23.47%
- Claude3.5-Sonnet: 35.56%

The evaluation included four open-source models: Qwen2-VL series (7B and 72B), InternVL2.5 variants (1B, 5B, 26B, 78B), and Llama-3.2-11B-Vision-Instruct.

## Setting Differences

The **oracle setting** provides models with "direct access to relevant context," while the **wikidoc setting** requires models to locate information "within extensive text" from full Wikipedia snapshots—simulating retrieval demands that reveal "significant" performance degradation.

Table 1 presents comprehensive results showing that proprietary models maintain ~70% accuracy with direct context but drop substantially in retrieval scenarios, whereas open-source models struggle in both conditions.

# DocLayout-YOLO Analysis

## (1) Training Datasets

DocLayout-YOLO uses **DocSynth-300K** as its primary pre-training dataset. This is a synthetically generated collection created through the Mesh-candidate BestFit algorithm. The paper states: *"Pre-training on the resulting DocSynth-300K dataset significantly improves fine-tuning performance across various document types."*

For fine-tuning and evaluation, the model is tested on:
- D4LA (11,092 images, 27 categories, 12 document types)
- DocLayNet (80,863 pages, 7 document types)
- DocStructBench (9,310 images across 4 subsets)

## (2) DocStructBench Performance by Category

| Subset | mAP | AP50 |
|--------|-----|------|
| Academic | 81.8 | 95.8 |
| Textbook | 73.7 | 90.3 |
| Market Analysis | 69.4 | 79.4 |
| Financial | 90.1 | 95.9 |

## (3) Non-Academic Document Coverage

Yes, the evaluation explicitly includes diverse document types beyond academic papers. DocStructBench comprises *"Academic, Textbooks, Market Analysis, and Financial"* subsets, representing "real-world scenario documents" from varied sources including publishers and websites.

## (4) Failure Cases and Distribution Shift

The paper briefly acknowledges limitations: *"For Market Analysis, DocLayout-YOLO is second best...we suspect this is because DocSynth-300K pre-training is still not sufficient for most complex layouts."*

However, detailed failure case analysis or systematic distribution shift discussion is absent from the paper.

## (5) Strong vs. Weak Performance Categories

**Strongest:** Financial documents (90.1 mAP) and Academic papers (81.8 mAP)

**Weakest:** Market Analysis reports (69.4 mAP), where the model underperforms compared to some baselines

It builds both a typed Logical Relation graph (LR graph: binary parent-child hierarchical edges) and a typed Spatial Relation graph (SR graph: 8-directional edges — top, bottom, left, right, top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right) over document element nodes including title, text, list, figure, table, table caption, and figure caption — the same node types LHEC uses. Its LoSpa model propagates via GCN to predict the index of the document element containing the answer (fully extractive: answer is OCR text retrieved from that region). GraphDoc (ICLR 2025) annotates spatial and logical relations (Up/Down/Left/Right, Parent/Child/Sequence) between document nodes, providing the taxonomy directly used in LHEC's rule-based edge assignment.

WikiMixQA (arXiv:2506.15594, ACL 2025 Findings) benchmarks within-page multi-hop reasoning over table+chart pairs from Wikipedia.
